page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable (Ice Lake 8375C) processors. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores operating at 3.5 GHz, supported by 54 MB of Level 3 cache along with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration. It includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB memory allocation per vCPU. Local storage features 5,700 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD instance storage, paired with a 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong multi-threaded and data-intensive throughput. The 96 vCPUs achieve upper-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng (92,925.60) and Geekbench multi-core (17,537.00), with PassMark encryption placing in the top 10 percent due to dedicated instruction support. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 329.87 GB/sec, while write operations sustain 139.61 GB/sec. In-memory data workloads perform well, demonstrated by 90.9 million Redis SET operations per second and 63.52 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-core performance falls in the average tier across stress-ng and compression suites, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel throughput over peak single-thread speeds.

Given its hardware configuration and high resource density, the r6idn.24xlarge provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput transaction processing systems. Bundling 5,700 GB of local NVMe storage alongside 150 Gbps networking eliminates separate storage provisioning overhead for scratchpad data and low-latency disk logging. However, without discrete GPUs, large language model generation throughput is limited. The server is suited for enterprise database clusters, Apache Spark or distributed analytics nodes, Redis or Memcached tiers, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
